newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC chief calls for transmission surcharge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC chief calls for transmission surcharge.

text.p: The new chairman of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday urged energy efficiency advocates to press Congress to give the commission the authority to collect a small transmission fee to help support energy conservation and other programs.

FERC chair James Hoecker said that as power markets were deregulated, the government ought to collect a small surcharge on all transmission to help pay for programs that utilities currently cover through their rates, such as low-income assistance, energy efficiency, and universal service.
"It would be extremely helpful ... to have this memorialized in legislation, as an amendment to the Federal Power Act," Hoecker said in his first speech as chairman of the commission.

"In an unbundled environment, our jurisdiction over transmission may tend to make it less practical ... for local utilities and state commissions to use distribution-based rates to fund a variety of programs," he said at an energy efficiency conference sponsored by Johnson Controls Inc and the U.S. Energy Association.
He said either the FERC or an independent board could be assigned to manage the funds raised from a transmission surcharge, using them to provide matching grants for benefits programs.
"I think it's a serious idea that's worth looking at," Hoecker said.
Hoecker was named chairman of the commission by President Bill Clinton this week to replace Elizabeth Moler, who left the agency to become deputy energy secretary.
In his speech, he reiterated his concerns about the wave of mergers in the utility industry.
"There's no question that the road to open and competitive markets contains some troubling obstacles," he said.

He said the growing number of mergers and consolidations among energy companies was "palpable evidence ... of designs to amass greater market share, if not market power, that insulates companies from competitive threats."
